key_insight: A steady boundary-driven flux can condense an otherwise stable binary mixture into a pinned annulus through an effective logarithmic field.
engineering_relevance: Permeate chemical potential and boundary permeability could control localized phase separation in radial membrane systems without changing the critical temperature.
method: Model B dynamics in a two-dimensional annulus with a semipermeable inner boundary.
Map the driven steady state to an equilibrium profile in an effective logarithmic field.
Derive condensation and interfacial-tension thresholds, then test predictions numerically.
evidence_signal: Numerical solutions confirm the analytical predictions and reveal hysteresis bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations.
watch_item: The results assume Model B dynamics and radial geometry; applicability with fluid flow or more complex boundaries remains untested in the abstract.
paper_title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
